title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: a fortiori never-could-live; interdict silence on posterity
pass_a_gloss: Still more: what of a span when the child not only lacked life but could not live at all, and a deed it neither did nor ever could do? Following the Apostle's habit in Galatians and Hebrews of weighing both what Scripture says and what it withholds, why miss that the Interdict and the post-fall sentence on Adam name no posterity? God already then left you no foothold for reading his justice your way.
pass_b_english: What then would he say of that time when the little child not only was not living life, but could not even live; and of a sin which it not only did not do, but never could do? But if by the Apostle's example in the Epistles to the Galatians and to the Hebrews we wish carefully to weigh Scripture's words and silence, what reason is there why we should not observe that in the Interdict, in the sentence pronounced to Adam after the interdict was violated, no mention of posterity was made? God already then took care, to be sure, lest he should offer you any handle for sensing concerning his justice as you do.
source_text: Quid ergo diceret de eo tempore quum puerulus non modo vita non vivebat, sed ne poterat quidem vivere; deque peccato quod non modo non fecit, sed neque potuit unquam facere? Quod si Apostoli exemplo in Epistolis ad Gal. & ad Heb. velimus Scripturae verba & silentium accurate perpendere, quid est quamobrem non observemus in Interdicto, in sententia post violatum interdictum Adamo pronunciata nullam esse posteritatis factam mentionem? Cavit nimirum Deus jam tum, ne vobis ullam praeberet ansam ita de justitia sua, ut facitis, sentiendi.
